convocatorias.title: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of energy intensive industries (IA) (Processes4Planet and Clean Steel partnerships) — 2026
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Proposals are expected to contribute to all the following expected outcomes: Accelerate the use of innovative technologies to decarbonise industrial processes and bring to the market more cost-effective clean products to strengthen the competitiveness, sustainability (including biodiversity), and resilience of EU industries; Create new innovative first-of-a-kind operational demonstrators and/or optimise newly installed industrial decarbonisation solutions in Europe; and Demonstrate the market readiness of the envisaged future clean products and their innovative processes via a credible business plan and an exploitation strategy for industrialisation, including market-tested use cases. Scope: The Clean Industrial Deal aims to secure the EU as an attractive location for manufacturing, including for energy-intensive industries, and to promote clean tech and new circular business models in order to meet Europe’s ambitious decarbonisation and climate neutrality targets. It focuses primarily on the competitive decarbonisation of EU industry and on the production of clean technologies in the EU. The following three technology areas on energy intensive industries having a strong and promising growth potential in Europe are in scope of this call: Managing of carbon cycle (CCU and/or CCUS): further optimization and demonstration of solutions for the capture, utilization or storage of CO2 and/or CO from installations of the energy intensive industries, with significant reduction of energy input (per ton of CO2/CO) related to capture rate and purity compared to current available technologies (target figure 30% reduction), and potential of commercialization of the decarbonized products with respect to LCA (compared to state of the art), market size, and cost. Clean energy usage in production (electrification of the processes, decarbonated production, integration of alternative clean energy carriers – e.g. hydrogen – and technologies, on-site renewable energy storage solutions, usage and upgrade of waste heat): supporting major improvements of clean energy usage in the energy intensive industries until 2035. Circularity and resource efficiency (material, energy, water) of production processes: improvement by 30% until 2035 compared to current industrial value, with technological solutions which are commercially viable; and significant reduction of the overall raw material consumption, energy input, freshwater intake, impact on ecosystems and emissions, through circular value networks that convert industrial side-streams and/or end-of-use waste to new feedstock for which no low-CO2-technologies currently exist. Solutions must have an overall positive LCA and remain commercially viable under the expected regulatory and framework conditions at the end of the project. Proposals should explicitly select one main area but can also address in an integrated way a combination of these three areas within an industrial sector, provided that it is innovative and can lead to low carbon solutions. The choice of the specific technologies addressed in the proposal is left to the project applicants who should include a thorough justification of the choices both in technological and business terms. Use of advanced, and safe and sustainable materials and processes could be also addressed as part of the selected proposals. Proposals are expected to: demonstrate an adequate integration of relevant technologies in support of the Clean Industrial Deal. The integration can either be demonstrated in a direct (e.g. reduction of greenhouse emissions of a process) or an indirect (e.g. production of a new green/clean product) manner. Reduction or avoidance of harmful pollutants and impact on biodiversity may also be considered, as relevant. [1] The use of relevant results of R&I projects previously or ongoing funded at EU, national or regional level is encouraged. show industrial leadership in the deployment after the project. To ensure market readiness and effective collaboration amongst relevant stakeholders, the consortium should be industry driven and composed of a preferably small and manageable number of participants, and its size should be justified. The participation of SMEs is encouraged. The draft dissemination, exploitation and communication plan is expected to include a sound and convincing business plan and market-readiness strategy (cf. intro). These should address how to prepare and support the deployment of the proposed tech solution across relevant EU industrial sectors, and/or how to ensure a high potential for market uptake through further private/public investment (including relevant EU deployment programmes, such as the Innovation Fund). They should include a comprehensive analysis of the critical barriers (technological and non-technological) for the successful market deployment and the corresponding plan to tackle them before 2030. Proposals are expected to include a clear go/no go moment ahead of the contracting and demonstration phase. Before this go/no-go moment, the project is expected to deliver detailed engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, all needed permits for the demonstrator, a complete business plan and market-readiness strategy, identifying clearly the industrial partner(s) that will lead the deployment. Proposals are also expected to provide a clear and credible pathway to obtaining all needed permits for the demonstration phase of the project. Taking into account that the Clean Industrial Deal focuses on clean tech and decarbonisation of energy-intensive industry , projects funded under this topic will be encouraged to develop synergies and coordinate on similar funded projects under the topics HORIZON-CID-2026-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action and HORIZON- HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action under this call, as well as with related projects funded under the Processess4Planet, and Clean Steel and other European Partnerships. This topic implements the co-programmed European partnerships Processes4Planet and Clean Steel. null Activities are expected to start at TRL 6 and achieve TRL 7 to 8 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. [1] For instance, biodiversity could be a priority in specific areas with significant impact on flora or fauna

convocatorias.org: Comisión Europea / Horizon Europe
convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: La convocatoria financia proyectos de I+D e innovación industrial (IA) para la descarbonización de industrias intensivas en energía en tres áreas tecnológicas: (1) Captura, utilización o almacenamiento de CO2/CO; (2) Uso de energía limpia en producción (electrificación, hidrógeno, almacenamiento renovable on-site, valorización de calor residual); (3) Circularidad y eficiencia de recursos (conversión de corrientes laterales y residuos en nuevas materias primas). Los proyectos deben partir de TRL 6 y alcanzar TRL 7-8 mediante demostradores operativos de primera aplicación industrial o soluciones de demostración optimizadas. Se financian costes de I+D, demostración, ingeniería, equipamiento, validación ambiental (LCA) y plan de explotación comercial. Se excluyen adquisiciones ordinarias sin innovación y proyectos sin viabilidad comercial o LCA positivo.
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa encaja como socio tecnológico o líder industrial en proyectos de demostración de tecnologías de recuperación y valorización de calor residual, electrificación de procesos térmicos e integración de hidrógeno en industrias intensivas en energía (cerámica, siderurgia, metalurgia, vidrio, química, cemento). La línea 'Clean energy usage in production' es la de mejor encaje (waste heat upgrade, electrificación, hidrógeno). La línea 'Circularity and resource efficiency' también es compatible si el proyecto integra valorización térmica de residuos. La línea CCU/CCUS tiene menor encaje sin evidencia de captura de CO2. Kalfrisa es elegible como empresa industrial de la UE. El consorcio es obligatorio y debe ser industry-driven; Kalfrisa debe asegurar socio industrial líder con instalación de demostración y entidades de investigación (CIRCE, Universidad de Zaragoza, CENER, CIEMAT) para LCA y validación. Quedan por verificar: presupuesto total, tasa de financiación, máximo de subvención, duración del proyecto, criterios de go/no go, y definición del caso de uso industrial específico.
convocatorias.action: Identificar inmediatamente socio industrial líder (empresa de energía intensiva con instalación de demostración disponible) y entidad de investigación para LCA. Desarrollar propuesta de proyecto en línea 'Clean energy usage in production' con foco en waste heat upgrade y/o electrificación + hidrógeno. Definir caso de uso concreto, TRL inicial (6) y TRL objetivo (7-8), plan de demostración, criterios de go/no go, y estrategia de explotación comercial. Verificar presupuesto, tasa de financiación y máximo de subvención Con la documentación oficial ya publicada la convocatoria (abierta desde 2025-12-18, cierre 2026-09-15). Preparar documentación de LCA y viabilidad comercial. Confirmar elegibilidad de todos los socios respecto a restricciones de CNAE, tamaño y tipo de entidad cuando se detallen en la convocatoria.

convocatorias.title: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action — 2026
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Proposals are expected to contribute to all the following expected outcomes: Strengthen the competitiveness, sustainability (including biodiversity) and resilience of an innovative clean tech solution by clearly demonstrating the capability to, significantly: increase its circular material use rate, based on a sound and realistic baseline; reduce the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) delivered to end-users - including, where relevant, production, distribution, and storage costs, based on a sound and realistic baseline and considering different geographic scenarios; and contribute to Europe’s industrial leadership and competitiveness, in line with the objectives of Net-Zero Industry Act (NZIA) [1] for the EU manufacturing capacity of net-zero technologies [2] , [3] . Bring this innovative clean tech solution to full technological maturity and close to market-readiness with a view to accelerating its market deployment and/or integration in key industrial sectors in Europe (e.g. manufacturing, energy and transport). Scope: The Clean Industrial Deal aims to secure the EU as an attractive location for manufacturing, including for energy-intensive industries, and to promote clean tech and new circular business models in order to meet Europe’s ambitious decarbonisation and climate neutrality and biodiversity preservation targets. It focuses primarily on the competitive decarbonisation of EU industry and on the production of clean technologies in the EU. This requires notably a considerable increase in electrification of EU energy systems and in all end-use sectors of the European economy (either directly, or via enabling intermediate technologies). The following three clean tech areas have a strong and promising growth potential in Europe. Proposals are expected to address one or several of these areas: Integrated net-zero emissions energy systems (e.g. including energy grids, networks and systems) Enhanced zero-emission power technologies (e.g. including renewable electricity, heat and energy technologies) Storage technologies, renewable fuels, and carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) (e.g. including batteries and other energy storage solutions, renewable hydrogen [4] , advanced biofuels and synthetic renewable fuels) enabling climate neutrality Proposals should explicitly select one main area but can also address in an integrated way a combination of these three areas. Applicants are free to decide on the specific value chain they wish to strengthen in the above clean tech areas. As part of bringing innovative clean tech solutions closer to the market, proposals may also address step-change in relevant network and infrastructure deployment to facilitate scale up across the trans-European energy and transport networks – e.g. electricity, heat, gas, hydrogen, CO2, batteries, and refuelling networks, etc. Application of advanced innovative materials development, connected process engineering and scale-up, resource efficiency, circularity and recycling may also be addressed as part of the selected value chain, as relevant. Attention should be paid to avoid technologies which may have a negative impact on biodiversity and ecosystems. Proposals are expected to: ensure the development of innovative technological solutions along a specific clean tech value chain. For this, they need to involve an adequate combination of clean tech suppliers, energy users (e.g. manufacturing, energy and transport) and other relevant stakeholders, in order to support a sound business case, taking into account a gender-sensitive and intersectional approach. demonstrate an adequate integration of relevant technological solutions including clean tech and industrial decarbonisation solutions in support of the Clean Industrial Deal, and to ensure a clear and quantifiable impact on competitiveness and reduction of GHG emissions. Reduction or avoidance of harmful pollutants and impact on biodiversity may also be considered, as relevant [5] . The integration can either be demonstrated in a direct (e.g. energy to an industrial/transport sector) or an indirect (e.g. energy to grid to an industrial/transport sector) manner. The use of relevant results of R&I projects previously or currently funded at EU or national level is encouraged. show industrial leadership in view of the deployment after the project. To ensure market readiness and effective collaboration amongst relevant stakeholders along a specific clean tech value chain, the consortium should be industry driven and composed of a manageable number of participants (indicatively, not more than ten participants). The consortium size should be justified based on the extent of the value chain covered. The participation of SMEs is encouraged. seek coherence with the work of the Strategic Energy Technology (SET) Plan and relevant industrial initiatives. The draft dissemination, exploitation and communication plan is expected to include a sound and convincing business plan and market-readiness strategy (cf. intro). They should address how to prepare and support the deployment of the proposed clean tech solution across relevant EU industrial sectors (e.g. energy, transport, manufacturing) and/or how to ensure a high potential for market uptake through further private/public investment (including relevant EU deployment programmes, such as the Innovation Fund). They should include a comprehensive analysis of the critical barriers (technological and non-technological) for the successful market deployment and the corresponding plan to address them. Proposals are expected to include a clear go/no go moment ahead of the contracting and demonstration phase. Before this go/no-go moment, the project is expected to deliver detailed engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, all needed permits for the demonstrator, a complete business plan and market-readiness strategy, identifying clearly the industrial partner(s) that will lead the deployment. Proposals are also expected to provide a clear and credible pathway to obtaining all needed permits for the demonstration phase of the project. Taking into account that the Clean Industrial Deal focuses on clean tech and energy-intensive industry decarbonisation, projects funded under this topic will be encouraged to develop synergies and coordinate with similar or complementary projects funded under the topics HORIZON-CID-2026-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of Energy Intensive Industries and HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of Energy Intensive Industries under this call, as well as with relevant projects funded under relevant European Partnerships (including e.g. the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking and the Clean Energy Transition Partnership). null Activities are expected to start at TRL 6 and achieve TRL 8 by the end of the project. convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: Horizon Europe financia proyectos de I+D e innovación en tecnologías limpias para la acción climática, dirigidos a fortalecer la competitividad industrial europea. La convocatoria cubre sistemas energéticos netos cero integrados, tecnologías de potencia cero emisiones, almacenamiento, combustibles renovables y captura de carbono. Los solicitantes definen libremente la cadena de valor específica dentro de estos temas. Se financian actividades de desarrollo tecnológico, demostración industrial y escalado desde TRL 6 a TRL 8. Los gastos elegibles incluyen I+D, ingeniería, construcción/adaptación de instalaciones piloto o demostrativas, equipamiento, validación y análisis de ciclo de vida. Se excluyen adquisiciones ordinarias sin innovación, investigación básica desvinculada de aplicación industrial y actividades fuera del alcance de tecnologías limpias. El consorcio debe ser dirigido por la industria, con máximo diez participantes; se alienta participación de PYME y reutilización de resultados de proyectos previos financiados en UE o nivel nacional.
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa, empresa industrial mediana con sede en Zaragoza (UE), es elegible como participante en esta convocatoria Horizon Europe de tecnologías limpias. Su cartera tecnológica (recuperación de calor residual, hornos de bajas emisiones, electrificación térmica, RTO, valorización de residuos, gemelos digitales) encaja directamente con los temas requeridos (sistemas energéticos netos cero, tecnologías de potencia cero emisiones, combustibles renovables). El rango TRL 6-8 es alcanzable desde su experiencia actual (TRL 4-7 con escalado). Línea aplicable: única, sin alternativas. Pendiente de verificación: (1) presupuesto total, tasa de financiación y máximo de subvención; (2) tipos de entidad y acciones elegibles en bases completas; (3) definición del rol específico en consorcio (líder tecnológico, fabricante/demostrador o socio industrial) y valor añadido diferenciado; (4) identificación y aseguramiento de socios complementarios (máximo diez) antes de propuesta; (5) plazo muy ajustado (27 días desde referencia 2026-08-20 hasta 2026-09-15).
convocatorias.action: Perseguir activamente. Acciones inmediatas: (1) Consultar bases completas de la convocatoria para confirmar presupuesto, tasa de financiación, tipos de entidad y acciones elegibles. (2) Definir propuesta de valor: seleccionar uno o varios de los tres temas (sistemas integrados netos cero, tecnologías de potencia cero emisiones, almacenamiento/combustibles renovables/CCU) y especificar cadena de valor y rol de Kalfrisa (líder tecnológico, fabricante/demostrador o socio industrial). (3) Identificar y contactar socios complementarios: priorizar CIRCE, CENER, CIEMAT, Universidad de Zaragoza I3A/LIFEn e ITE para investigación/LCA; buscar socio industrial de sector clave (cerámica, siderurgia, metalurgia, vidrio, química, cemento) para demostración; asegurar coordinador con experiencia Horizon Europe. (4) Evaluar reutilización de resultados de HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, EDPIC, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO, RAFeRTO, DT4RAF, IGNITE y documentación requerida. (5) Movilizar equipo de propuesta inmediatamente: plazo de 27 días es crítico. (6) Revisar sinergia con HORIZON-CID-2026-01-02 y HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02 para evitar solapamiento. (7) Preparar presupuesto preliminar y plan de trabajo alineado con TRL 6-8 y objetivos de competitividad, circularidad y despliegue de mercado.

convocatorias.title: Full-scale demonstration of heat upgrade solutions in industrial processes
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following expected outcomes: Based on the results of the project, at least one industrial sector with a significant heating demand in the EU and Associated Countries develops pathways and business models to measurably increase the recovery and upgrade of locally available heat for covering process needs and significantly or totally phasing out of fossil fuel use, while preserving or enhancing its global competitiveness. Measurable improvement of renewable and/or industrial excess/waste heat recovery and upgrade solutions, possibly combined with thermal and/or electrical energy storage, in terms of energy efficiency, flexibility of electrical demand, climate and environment protection, reliability and safety, physical and cyber security, and profitability. Scope: This topic aims to satisfy the need for process heat in the more industrial sectors by upgrading excess/waste heat from the process itself, possibly combined with heat recovered in nearby locations or local renewable heat, as a cost-efficient way to improve energy efficiency and reduce the GHG emissions and air pollutants and the use of fossil fuels. Thermal and/or electrical energy storage can be integrated, if it can contribute to better matching heat sources with process needs and/or to offer more flexible electricity consumption from the grid. The temperature of the heat supplied to the process is not specified, but the proposals will be evaluated on their potential to enable the deployment of heat upgrade solutions in more sector(s) and process(es), where they are not yet state-of-the art. Projects must address all the following items: Optimise and demonstrate physically within one or more operational industrial site(s), the transformation of process(es) in at least one industrial sector, by recovering excess/waste heat from the process itself, possibly combined with local renewable heat or heat recovered in nearby locations and local thermal and/or electrical energy storage, and by upgrading the heat (e.g. with heat pump) for use in the process(es). Maximise the replicability and deployment of the concept/solution in the EU and Associated Countries’ plants in the same industrial sector. Already before starting the design phase, the needs of most EU and Associated Countries’ factories in the same industrial sector(s) should be surveyed and analysed in order to design a solution that can be adapted to meet most of them. Identify common components, optimise and define a standardised version of them. Develop open technical and economical guidelines and open tools for system design and business case development. In case the targeted industrial sector(s) and process(es) has/have been covered by the actions under the topic LIFE-2024-CET-HEATPUMPS [1] , this proposal should build on the results of these actions and if possible, cooperate with them, both for the definition of the solution to demonstrate and the dissemination channels. Disseminate results notably (but not only) to the relevant communities in cluster 4 ‘Digital, Industry and Space’ private-public partnerships and to JRC Sevilla and INCITE for work on BREFs in the context of the IED2.0. null Activities are expected to achieve TRL 7-8 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. Activities may start at any TRL. [1] https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/life-2024-cet-heatpumps

Tipo de entidad elegible no especificado en hechos. Riesgo: si la convocatoria exige consorcios con investigación pública o centros de investigación como líderes, Kalfrisa podría quedar limitada a rol de socio industrial sin acceso a financiación directa.

convocatorias.title: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of energy intensive industries (IA) (Processes4Planet and Clean Steel partnerships) — 2027
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Proposals are expected to contribute to all the following expected outcomes: Accelerate the use of innovative technologies to decarbonise industrial processes and bring to the market more cost-effective clean products to strengthen the competitiveness, sustainability (including biodiversity), and resilience of EU industries; Create new innovative first-of-a-kind operational demonstrators and/or optimise newly installed industrial decarbonisation solutions in Europe; and Demonstrate the market readiness of the envisaged future clean products and their innovative processes via a credible business plan and an exploitation strategy for industrialisation, including market-tested use cases. Scope: The Clean Industrial Deal aims to secure the EU as an attractive location for manufacturing, including for energy-intensive industries, and to promote clean tech and new circular business models in order to meet Europe’s ambitious decarbonisation and climate neutrality targets. It focuses primarily on the competitive decarbonisation of EU industry and on the production of clean technologies in the EU. The following three technology areas on energy intensive industries having a strong and promising growth potential in Europe are in scope of this call: Managing of carbon cycle (CCU and/or CCUS): further optimization and demonstration of solutions for the capture, utilization or storage of CO2 and/or CO from installations of the energy intensive industries, with significant reduction of energy input (per ton of CO2/CO) related to capture rate and purity compared to current available technologies (target figure 30% reduction), and potential of commercialization of the decarbonized products with respect to LCA (compared to state of the art), market size, and cost. Clean energy usage in production (electrification of the processes, decarbonated production, integration of alternative clean energy carriers – e.g. hydrogen – and technologies, on-site renewable energy storage solutions, usage and upgrade of waste heat): supporting major improvements of clean energy usage in the energy intensive industries until 2035. Circularity and resource efficiency (material, energy, water) of production processes: improvement by 30% until 2035 compared to current industrial value, with technological solutions which are commercially viable; and significant reduction of the overall raw material consumption, energy input, freshwater intake, impact on ecosystems and emissions, through circular value networks that convert industrial side-streams and/or end-of-use waste to new feedstock for which no low-CO2-technologies currently exist. Solutions must have an overall positive LCA and remain commercially viable under the expected regulatory and framework conditions at the end of the project. Proposals should explicitly select one main area but can also address in an integrated way a combination of these three areas within an industrial sector, provided that it is innovative and can lead to low carbon solutions. The choice of the specific technologies addressed in the proposal is left to the project applicants who should include a thorough justification of the choices both in technological and business terms. Use of advanced, and safe and sustainable materials and processes could be also addressed as part of the selected proposals. Proposals are expected to: demonstrate an adequate integration of relevant technologies in support of the Clean Industrial Deal. The integration can either be demonstrated in a direct (e.g. reduction of greenhouse emissions of a process) or an indirect (e.g. production of a new green/clean product) manner. Reduction or avoidance of harmful pollutants and impact on biodiversity may also be considered, as relevant. [1] The use of relevant results of R&I projects previously or ongoing funded at EU, national or regional level is encouraged. show industrial leadership in the deployment after the project. To ensure market readiness and effective collaboration amongst relevant stakeholders, the consortium should be industry driven and composed of a preferably small and manageable number of participants, and its size should be justified. The participation of SMEs is encouraged. The draft dissemination, exploitation and communication plan is expected to include a sound and convincing business plan and market-readiness strategy (cf. intro). These should address how to prepare and support the deployment of the proposed tech solution across relevant EU industrial sectors, and/or how to ensure a high potential for market uptake through further private/public investment (including relevant EU deployment programmes, such as the Innovation Fund). They should include a comprehensive analysis of the critical barriers (technological and non-technological) for the successful market deployment and the corresponding plan to tackle them before 2030. Proposals are expected to include a clear go/no go moment ahead of the contracting and demonstration phase. Before this go/no-go moment, the project is expected to deliver detailed engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, all needed permits for the demonstrator, a complete business plan and market-readiness strategy, identifying clearly the industrial partner(s) that will lead the deployment. Proposals are also expected to provide a clear and credible pathway to obtaining all needed permits for the demonstration phase of the project. Taking into account that the Clean Industrial Deal focuses on clean tech and decarbonisation of energy-intensive industry , projects funded under this topic will be encouraged to develop synergies and coordinate on similar funded projects under the topics HORIZON-CID-2026-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action and HORIZON- HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action under this call, as well as with related projects funded under the Processess4Planet, and Clean Steel and other European Partnerships. This topic implements the co-programmed European partnerships Processes4Planet and Clean Steel. null Activities are expected to start at TRL 6 and achieve TRL 7 to 8 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: La convocatoria financia demostraciones industriales de primer tipo (first-of-a-kind) y optimización de soluciones de descarbonización en industrias intensivas en energía, en tres líneas: (1) captura, utilización o almacenamiento de CO2/CO con reducción de energía ≥30% respecto a tecnologías disponibles; (2) electrificación de procesos, integración de portadores energéticos limpios (hidrógeno), almacenamiento renovable on-site y valorización de calor residual; (3) mejora de circularidad y eficiencia de recursos con reducción ≥30% hasta 2035 y viabilidad comercial bajo LCA positivo. Su experiencia en demostraciones industriales (HIGH2-FURNACES, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO) y gemelos digitales encaja con el objetivo de optimizar soluciones de descarbonización en industrias intensivas en energía. convocatorias.title: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action — 2027
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Proposals are expected to contribute to all the following expected outcomes: Strengthen the competitiveness, sustainability (including biodiversity) and resilience of an innovative clean tech solution by clearly demonstrating the capability to, significantly: increase its circular material use rate, based on a sound and realistic baseline; reduce the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) delivered to end-users - including, where relevant, production, distribution, and storage costs, based on a sound and realistic baseline and considering different geographic scenarios; and contribute to Europe’s industrial leadership and competitiveness, in line with the objectives of Net-Zero Industry Act (NZIA) [1] for the EU manufacturing capacity of net-zero technologies [2] , [3] . Bring this innovative clean tech solution to full technological maturity and close to market-readiness with a view to accelerating its market deployment and/or integration in key industrial sectors in Europe (e.g. manufacturing, energy and transport). Scope: The Clean Industrial Deal aims to secure the EU as an attractive location for manufacturing, including for energy-intensive industries, and to promote clean tech and new circular business models in order to meet Europe’s ambitious decarbonisation and climate neutrality and biodiversity preservation targets. It focuses primarily on the competitive decarbonisation of EU industry and on the production of clean technologies in the EU. This requires notably a considerable increase in electrification of EU energy systems and in all end-use sectors of the European economy (either directly, or via enabling intermediate technologies). The following three clean tech areas have a strong and promising growth potential in Europe. Proposals are expected to address one or several of these areas: Integrated net-zero emissions energy systems (e.g. including energy grids, networks and systems) Enhanced zero-emission power technologies (e.g. including renewable electricity, heat and energy technologies) Storage technologies, renewable fuels, and carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) (e.g. including batteries and other energy storage solutions, renewable hydrogen [4] , advanced biofuels and synthetic renewable fuels) enabling climate neutrality Proposals should explicitly select one main area but can also address in an integrated way a combination of these three areas. Applicants are free to decide on the specific value chain they wish to strengthen in the above clean tech areas. As part of bringing innovative clean tech solutions closer to the market, proposals may also address step-change in relevant network and infrastructure deployment to facilitate scale up across the trans-European energy and transport networks – e.g. electricity, heat, gas, hydrogen, CO2, batteries, and refuelling networks, etc. Application of advanced innovative materials development, connected process engineering and scale-up, resource efficiency, circularity and recycling may also be addressed as part of the selected value chain, as relevant. Attention should be paid to avoid technologies which may have a negative impact on biodiversity and ecosystems. Proposals are expected to: ensure the development of innovative technological solutions along a specific clean tech value chain. For this, they need to involve an adequate combination of clean tech suppliers, energy users (e.g. manufacturing, energy and transport) and other relevant stakeholders, in order to support a sound business case, taking into account a gender-sensitive and intersectional approach. demonstrate an adequate integration of relevant technological solutions including clean tech and industrial decarbonisation solutions in support of the Clean Industrial Deal, and to ensure a clear and quantifiable impact on competitiveness and reduction of GHG emissions. Reduction or avoidance of harmful pollutants and impact on biodiversity may also be considered, as relevant [5] . The integration can either be demonstrated in a direct (e.g. energy to an industrial/transport sector) or an indirect (e.g. energy to grid to an industrial/transport sector) manner. The use of relevant results of R&I projects previously or currently funded at EU or national level is encouraged. show industrial leadership in view of the deployment after the project. To ensure market readiness and effective collaboration amongst relevant stakeholders along a specific clean tech value chain, the consortium should be industry driven and composed of a manageable number of participants (indicatively, not more than ten participants). The consortium size should be justified based on the extent of the value chain covered. The participation of SMEs is encouraged. seek coherence with the work of the Strategic Energy Technology (SET) Plan and relevant industrial initiatives. The draft dissemination, exploitation and communication plan is expected to include a sound and convincing business plan and market-readiness strategy (cf. intro). They should address how to prepare and support the deployment of the proposed clean tech solution across relevant EU industrial sectors (e.g. energy, transport, manufacturing) and/or how to ensure a high potential for market uptake through further private/public investment (including relevant EU deployment programmes, such as the Innovation Fund). They should include a comprehensive analysis of the critical barriers (technological and non-technological) for the successful market deployment and the corresponding plan to address them. Proposals are expected to include a clear go/no go moment ahead of the contracting and demonstration phase. Before this go/no-go moment, the project is expected to deliver detailed engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, all needed permits for the demonstrator, a complete business plan and market-readiness strategy, identifying clearly the industrial partner(s) that will lead the deployment. Proposals are also expected to provide a clear and credible pathway to obtaining all needed permits for the demonstration phase of the project. Taking into account that the Clean Industrial Deal focuses on clean tech and energy-intensive industry decarbonisation, projects funded under this topic will be encouraged to develop synergies and coordinate with similar or complementary projects funded under the topics HORIZON-CID-2026-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of Energy Intensive Industries and HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02: R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Decarbonisation of Energy Intensive Industries under this call, as well as with relevant projects funded under relevant European Partnerships (including e.g. the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking and the Clean Energy Transition Partnership). null Activities are expected to start at TRL 6 and achieve TRL 8 by the end of the projec. [1] Net-Zero Industry Act: resource.html [2] This should apply to each main specific component of the project for which, under the NZIA, it is established that more than 50% of Union’s supply originates from a third country. In such cases, at least 50% of these components should be sourced from the EU or other Horizon Europe Associated Countries. In cases where a strong dependency would compromise the viability of the project, beneficiaries may aim at a lower percentage providing an adequate justification in the proposal. [3] 860c257b-16db-429e-91c1-a30bea57e7ce_en [4] Projects need to ensure complementarities with the activities under the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking [5] For instance, biodiversity could be a priority in specific areas with significant impact on flora or fauna.

convocatorias.title: Efficient energy input from renewable sources and energy management in the process industries (IA) (Processes4Planet and Innovative Advanced Materials for the EU partnerships)
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: A significant decarbonisation of processes (measured by the reduction of GHG emissions from the overall system) with broad applicability and economic viability. Facilitation of the transition from fossil-based energy inputs for: low/medium thermal energy demands by introducing renewable-based alternatives and heat upgrading. High-temperature processes, by innovative technologies for electrified and hybrid high-temperature processes, high temperature energy storage. Clean energy usage is given a boost through innovative advanced materials, system concepts and technologies for energy integration and energy storage, supporting resilience against energy supply variations Combination of significant energy savings and integrated management of energy systems and production processes Scope: Most processes in the process industries require significant energy inputs which currently lead to substantial CO2 emissions by the process industries. The reduction of the CO2 footprint can be achieved by several measures, e.g. electrification or use of other renewable sources of energy, lowering of the energy demand, increasing energy efficiency, and energy integration. This topic aims to lead to significant steps in reducing the CO2 footprint by technological innovations, at least by 20%. A key problem in the use of renewable energy sources is their fluctuation over time. Projects should take this into account and develop solutions that aim for energy efficiency and include novel storage technologies of relevance to the process industries. Pure demand-side management by production schedules adapted to the supply of electricity from renewable sources is not within the scope of the call. In situations where full electrification is not feasible or competitive in the foreseeable future, sustainable hybrid solutions play a crucial role. These solutions enhance flexibility, allowing industries to manage the variability in the availability of affordable renewable electricity, which is expected to fluctuate significantly in the medium term. E.g., preheating processes can utilize fossil-free energy sources such as solar heat, geothermal heat, heat pumps, resistive or induction heating, and electric boilers. This initial stage can be followed by further heating using fossil-based methods initially, and later transitioning to renewable-based combustion processes to achieve the required process temperatures. To enhance resilience, the capture, storage, and management of energy flows should be tailored to the needs of the process industry. This may include research and innovation in safe and sustainable innovative advanced materials for (latent or sensible) energy storage, e.g. phase change materials and heat storage via chemical energy carriers beyond E-fuels. Proposals under this topic should address several of the following: Advancements in the use of energy from renewable sources in production processes with improved energy efficiency. Integrated energy systems with novel storage elements to enable a smooth operation of the plants despite variations in the availability of energy from renewable sources. Solutions for low/medium temperature (100 - 500 °C) energy inputs in energy intensive industries including hybrid solutions and a progressive reduction of the use of fossil carriers of energy. Solutions for high temperature (> 500 °C) energy inputs in energy intensive industries, including high temperature electricity driven processes, and high temperature energy storage. Application of high-performance insulation materials and new innovative advanced materials that can improve heat capture, storage, and retrieval, particularly for scalable high-temperature applications. Such materials should minimize the use of critical raw material, enabling effective recycling. Projects should include demonstrations at pilot scale, preferably in real industrial environments, to validate the proposed technologies and processes under real-world industrial conditions Proposals related to innovative advanced materials development should address the most relevant gaps to focus on in the frame from materials design to technology deployment and ensure adequate feedback loops between different steps to drive forward innovative solutions which can be easily deployed. Scalability and requirements from application/industry need to be considered early on in the innovation process. The inclusion of a GHG avoidance methodology [1] is recommended and should provide detailed descriptions of baselines and projected emissions reduction. Proposals should include a business case and exploitation strategy, as outlined in the introduction to this Destination, underlining how the proposal will serve the purpose to boost industrial decarbonisation technologies supply chain in Europe. As project output an elaborated exploitation plan should be developed, including preliminary plans for scalability, commercialisation and deployment (feasibility study, business plan and financial model) indicating possible private and public funding sources (e.g. Innovation Fund, InvestEU and cohesion policy funds). Societal- and environmental impact as well as implications for the workplace (including skills and organisational change) should be outlined. This topic implements the co-programmed European partnerships Processes4Planet and Innovative Advanced Materials for the EU. null Activities are expected to start at TRL 4-5 and achieve TRL 6-7 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. [1] That could follow Innovation Fund methodology: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/innovfund/wp-call/2021/call-annex_c_innovfund-lsc-2021_en.pdf

convocatorias.title: Demonstration of industrial excess/waste heat conversion to mechanical or electrical power
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following expected outcomes: Based on the results of the project, at least one industrial sector with a significant heating demand in the EU and Associated Countries develops pathways and business models to measurably increase the industrial excess/waste heat recovery and conversion to power. Measurable improvement of industrial excess/waste heat recovery and conversion to power, possibly combined with energy storage, in terms of energy efficiency, flexibility of electricity production, climate and environment protection, reliability and safety, physical and cyber security, and profitability. Scope: Better use of process excess/waste heat represents a significant source of energy savings for industries. The conversion of excess heat back to electricity, would improve energy efficiency, mitigate the increase of electricity consumption due to industrial electrification, as well as offer flexible electricity generation to stabilise the grid, if combined with thermal and/or electrical energy storage. Projects must address all the following items: Develop and validate novel excess/waste heat recovery and conversion systems. Demonstrate physically within one or more operational industrial site(s), the recovery of industrial excess/waste heat, possibly combined with energy storage, and its conversion to mechanical or electrical power. Maximise the replicability and deployment of the concept/solution in the EU and Associated Countries’ plants in the same industrial sector. Already before starting the design phase, the needs of most EU and Associated Countries’ factories in the same industrial sector(s) should be surveyed and analysed in order to design a solution that can be adapted to meet most of them. Identify common components, optimise and define a standardised version of them. Develop open technical and economical guidelines and open tools for integrating such systems into SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) and EMS (Energy Management System) infrastructures of existing plants, and for developing innovative business model of heat valorisation as a flexible electricity generation offered to stabilise the power grid. Disseminate results notably (but not only) to the relevant communities in cluster 4 ‘Digital, Industry and Space’ private-public partnerships. null Activities are expected to achieve TRL 7-8 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. Activities may start at any TRL.

Replicabilidad y estandarización de componentes: la convocatoria exige 'versiones estandarizadas' e 'integración en SCADA/EMS'. Kalfrisa debe demostrar capacidad de modularización y transferencia tecnológica, no solo demostración puntual.
partner_needs: Socio académico/investigación para validación de modelos CFD/HPC y análisis de ciclo de vida (LCA) vinculado a recuperadores y sistemas de conversión.
Socio industrial en sector de demanda térmica significativa (cerámica, metalurgia, química, refractarios) para demostración en planta real y análisis de necesidades de fábrica.
Socio especializado en integración SCADA/EMS y ciberseguridad para desarrollo de directrices técnicas y económicas de integración en infraestructuras existentes.

convocatorias.socio_consorcio: CIRCE, TECNALIA, Universidad de Zaragoza — I3A/LIFEn
convocatorias.org: Comisión Europea / Horizon Europe
convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: La convocatoria financia el desarrollo, validación y demostración de sistemas innovadores de recuperación y conversión de calor residual industrial a potencia mecánica o eléctrica en sectores con demanda significativa de calefacción en la UE y países asociados. Financia actividades de encuesta y análisis de necesidades de fábricas, identificación de componentes comunes y versiones estandarizadas, desarrollo de directrices técnicas y económicas para integración en infraestructuras SCADA/EMS, y desarrollo de modelos de negocio de valorización térmica como generación flexible de electricidad. Excluye explícitamente investigación básica (TRL 1-3) sin ruta industrial clara; requiere TRL 7-8 al cierre del proyecto. No constan exclusiones explícitas de gastos, pero la elegibilidad de costes se rige por las normas de Horizon Europe (costes directos e indirectos de I+D, demostración, validación y análisis de replicabilidad).
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa presenta alineación tecnológica fuerte (recuperación de calor residual, electrificación térmica, gemelos digitales) con el scope de HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D4-09, que busca sistemas innovadores de conversión de calor residual a potencia. La experiencia en proyectos como HIGH2-FURNACES, LIFE ABATE y e-RTO respalda capacidad de demostración industrial. Sin embargo, la elegibilidad formal es desconocida: no constan tipos de entidad elegibles, restricciones por tamaño, ni si se admiten solicitantes individuales o se exige consorcio. El TRL mínimo esperado (7-8 al cierre) requiere verificación de madurez actual de tecnologías candidatas, dado que el perfil declara TRL preferente 4-7. Presupuesto total, tasa de financiación y grant máximo no están especificados, impidiendo evaluar viabilidad económica. La convocatoria abre el 2027-05-05 y cierra el 2027-09-15; Kalfrisa debe preparar candidatura identificando sector industrial específico, tecnología madura (TRL ≥7 o con ruta clara a TRL 7-8), y potenciales socios académicos e industriales para validación, demostración y análisis de replicabilidad. Recomendación: seguimiento activo hasta publicación de bases completas; no actuar hasta confirmar elegibilidad y presupuesto.
convocatorias.action: Monitorizar publicación de bases completas de HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D4-09 (apertura prevista 2027-05-05). Verificar: (1) tipos de entidad elegibles y restricciones por tamaño; (2) si se admiten solicitantes individuales o consorcio obligatorio; (3) presupuesto total, tasa de cofinanciación y grant máximo; (4) TRL mínimo al inicio vs. al cierre (si es flexible o fijo). Identificar internamente tecnología de recuperación/conversión de calor residual con TRL actual ≥6 y ruta clara a TRL 7-8 en plazo de proyecto. Contactar a CIRCE (Aragón, waste_heat + industrial_electrification) y Universidad de Zaragoza I3A/LIFEn (waste_heat, validación CFD/LCA) para explorar liderazgo compartido o participación como socio tecnológico. Identificar sector industrial piloto (cerámica, metalurgia, química, refractarios) con demanda térmica significativa en Aragón o España para demostración. Preparar propuesta de valor en torno a estandarización de componentes y modelos de negocio de valorización térmica flexible. Plazo: iniciar contactos 2027-04 para candidatura en 2027-05-2027-09.

convocatorias.title: Proyectos de I+D — Línea PID (ventanilla abierta)
convocatorias.description: Financiación de proyectos empresariales de investigación industrial y desarrollo experimental para la creación o mejora significativa de procesos productivos, productos o servicios. Presupuesto mínimo 175.000 €. Ayuda parcialmente reembolsable hasta el 85% con tramo no reembolsable del 10-33%. Modalidad individual, cooperación nacional e internacional. Aplica directamente a proyectos de eficiencia térmica, control de emisiones y combustión industrial H2-ready de Kalfrisa.
convocatorias.eligibility_reason: La convocatoria CDTI PID no especifica tipos de entidad elegibles, CNAE admisibles ni geografías restringidas en los hechos extraídos. Kalfrisa (CNAE 2899, empresa mediana, Zaragoza) encaja potencialmente en modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) y en acciones de I+D industrial y desarrollo experimental. (2) si CNAE 2899 (fabricación de máquinas y equipos) es explícitamente elegible; (3) estado actual de la ventanilla abierta y plazo de presentación vigente.
positive_evidence: Kalfrisa posee capacidades en recuperación de calor residual, hornos industriales, combustión con hidrógeno (hasta 100% H2) y electrificación de procesos térmicos, alineadas con etiquetas hydrogen_combustion y energy_efficiency de la convocatoria.
Experiencia demostrada en proyectos I+D (HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, EDPIC, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO, RAFeRTO, DT4RAF, IGNITE) con TRL 4-7 y demostraciones industriales.
Modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) permite a Kalfrisa actuar como solicitante único si el presupuesto mínimo (175.000 €) se alcanza.
Acciones elegibles (investigación industrial, desarrollo experimental, mejora de procesos y productos) coinciden con el portafolio de I+D de Kalfrisa.
Tasa de financiación del 85% con componente no reembolsable (10-33%) es atractiva para proyectos de demostración industrial.
risks_and_unknowns: Estado de la convocatoria marcado como 'unknown' en los hechos; aunque se indica 'ventanilla abierta' y 'deterministic_call_status: open', no constan fecha de apertura, plazo de cierre ni confirmación de vigencia a 2026-08-20.
No se especifican tipos de entidad elegibles ni CNAE admisibles; no puede confirmarse que CNAE 2899 sea explícitamente aceptado.
Presupuesto mínimo de 175.000 € es conocido, pero no constan máximos ni distribución de costes elegibles (personal, equipos, subcontratación, etc.).
TRL mínimo y máximo no especificados; aunque Kalfrisa opera preferentemente en TRL 4-7, no se confirma si la línea acepta este rango.

Modalidad individual viable, pero si Kalfrisa requiere socios (p. ej., para validación, certificación o escalado), la modalidad de cooperación nacional (consorcio obligatorio) sería alternativa; ambas comparten condiciones base.
Geografía: no consta restricción a España, pero CDTI es financiador nacional; se asume elegibilidad de beneficiarios españoles sin confirmación explícita.
partner_needs: Validación de seguridad y rendimiento en combustión con hidrógeno: CIDAUT (combustion, hydrogen_combustion) o Fundación Hidrógeno Aragón (hydrogen_safety, hydrogen_supply).
Análisis de ciclo de vida (LCA) y sistemas energéticos: CIRCE, CENER o CIEMAT (energy_systems, lca).
Investigación en combustión y caracterización de mezclas H2: Universidad de Zaragoza — I3A/LIFEn (hydrogen_combustion, lca).
Si el proyecto incluye recuperación de calor y eficiencia energética, socios con expertise en sistemas energéticos (CIRCE, CENER, CIEMAT) reforzarían la propuesta.

convocatorias.title: Fast Track to Innovation for breakthroughs in the Chemical Industry Action Plan  (Research and Innovation Action)
convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Proposals should describe a credible pathway from their project results and outcomes towards the expected impact of this Destination; Enable the acceleration of the market uptake of groundbreaking innovations in the decarbonisation of the chemical industries as well as alternatives to substances of concern. Scope: This open topic aims to speed up the adoption of new, groundbreaking innovations (starting TRL 4 ) as part of the Chemical Industry Action Plan, in the areas of decarbonisation of energy intensive industries, circular economy or breakthrough production technologies; as well as development of alternatives (new chemical substances, advanced materials or technologies) to substances of concern. Application of the SSbD Framework should be considered as appropriate.
convocatorias.eligibility_reason: La convocatoria no publica tipos de solicitantes elegibles, geografías, entidades excluidas ni criterios de elegibilidad explícitos. Horizon Europe admite típicamente beneficiarios de la UE, pero faltan datos sobre restricciones por tamaño, CNAE, vinculación o exclusiones específicas de esta acción. Debe verificarse contra el texto completo de la convocatoria cuando esté disponible (apertura: 2026-09-22).
positive_evidence: Kalfrisa posee experiencia demostrada en decarbonización de procesos térmicos industriales (HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, IGNITE, LIFE ABATE).
Capacidades en recuperación de calor residual, combustión con hidrógeno y electrificación de calor de proceso alineadas con decarbonización de industrias intensivas en energía.
TRL mínimo 4 coincide con el punto de partida de la acción; experiencia en TRL 4-7 y demostraciones industriales.
Sectores de aplicación (química, metalurgia, cerámica, vidrio, refractarios) incluyen industrias químicas objetivo de la acción.
Ubicación en Aragón (España) compatible con Horizon Europe si se confirma elegibilidad de beneficiarios españoles en esta acción.
risks_and_unknowns: Convocatoria aún no abierta (apertura: 2026-09-22); texto completo y criterios de elegibilidad no disponibles.
No constan tipos de solicitantes elegibles, geografías, restricciones por tamaño, CNAE o exclusiones explícitas.

No se especifica si se admiten solicitantes individuales o si es obligatorio consorcio; no consta presupuesto total, tasa de financiación, coste mínimo/máximo de proyecto ni dotación máxima de subvención.
No se detalla si Kalfrisa podría actuar como beneficiaria principal (líder) o solo como socio tecnológico en consorcio.

Alcance de 'breakthrough production technologies' y 'alternatives to substances of concern' no definido; riesgo de que la innovación requerida supere el TRL 4-7 preferente de Kalfrisa o exija tecnologías fuera de su perfil.
Mención de 'SSbD Framework' sin contexto: si implica restricciones de sustancias o diseño específico, requiere verificación de compatibilidad con procesos de Kalfrisa.
partner_needs: Socio de investigación/LCA para evaluación de ciclo de vida y sostenibilidad (CIRCE, CENER, CIEMAT, Universidad de Zaragoza I3A/LIFEn).
Socio de sistemas energéticos para modelado de integración en cadenas de valor químicas (CIRCE, CENER, CIEMAT, ITE).
Potencial socio industrial químico o de proceso si Kalfrisa actúa como proveedor tecnológico de equipos/sistemas de decarbonización.

convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: La convocatoria financia proyectos de I+D+i en innovación de procesos y organización en industria manufacturera mediante subvención sin contraprestación. Admite investigación industrial, desarrollo experimental e innovación en procesos (mejora de métodos de producción, aplicación de técnicas/equipos/sistemas, modificación significativa de operaciones con mejoras medibles en productividad, calidad, sostenibilidad, fiabilidad o reducción de costes). (2) elegibilidad geográfica (sede en Zaragoza vs. requisito Navarra); (3) TRL mínimo/máximo no especificado en convocatoria; (4) retos del anexo I.A para línea estratégica; (5) funding rate y máximo subvención.
convocatorias.action: Solicitar a Kalfrisa: según normativa Navarra; (b) confirmación de si proyecto puede ejecutarse en Navarra o si ubicación de beneficiario es requisito; socio compatible con capacidades térmicas/industriales; (e) consultar anexo I.A para alineación con retos estratégicos si se considera línea estratégica. Financia actuaciones de investigación, desarrollo e innovación en procesos térmicos industriales mediante ayuda parcialmente reembolsable. Excluye explícitamente proyectos sin socio internacional y, por naturaleza de CDTI, adquisición ordinaria de equipos sin componente innovadora.
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa encaja tecnológicamente en línea CDTI de combustión industrial y eficiencia térmica: experiencia en recuperación de calor, hornos de bajas emisiones, hibridación H2 y gemelos digitales alinea con objeto de convocatoria. Línea aplicable es Proyectos Bilaterales CDTI, permanente hasta 2026-12-31. Rol recomendado: socio tecnológico o demostrador industrial. Pendientes de verificación crítica: (1) elegibilidad de empresa mediana española bajo criterios CDTI no especificados en fuente; (2) presupuesto máximo, cofinanciación y rango de coste de proyecto; (3) rango TRL aceptado; (4) identificación y compromiso de socio internacional europeo (requisito obligatorio); (5) temas/acciones elegibles específicas dentro de combustión e eficiencia térmica.
convocatorias.action: Solicitar a CDTI: (a) bases reguladoras completas de Proyectos Bilaterales 2026 con especificación de tipos de entidad, presupuestos, TRL y geografías elegibles; (b) ejemplos de proyectos financiados en combustión industrial y recuperación de calor para validar alineación; (c) identificar y pre-comprometer socio internacional europeo con capacidad en sistemas energéticos o modelización térmica antes de redacción de propuesta. Evaluar internamente si rol de Kalfrisa es líder (requiere presupuesto mayor) o socio tecnológico (menor riesgo administrativo). Reactivar evaluación una vez confirmados presupuesto, TRL y elegibilidad de entidad.

Financia actuaciones de I+D industrial en el área prioritaria 'Transición Energética' con coste mínimo de 175.000 € y subcontratación mínima del 10% al Centro Tecnológico colaborador. convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa presenta alineación tecnológica significativa con 'Transición Energética' (recuperación de calor residual, electrificación térmica, hibridación con hidrógeno, RTO, valorización térmica de residuos, gemelos digitales). Pendientes de verificación crítica: (1) plazo abierto y vigente a 2026-08-20; (2) identificación de Centro Tecnológico acreditado socio obligatorio; (3) confirmación de rol de Kalfrisa (solicitante principal vs. socio industrial); (4) presupuesto máximo de proyecto y TRL admitidos; (5) geografía elegible.
convocatorias.action: Solicitar a gestor de convocatorias: (a) confirmación de plazo abierto y fecha límite actual; (b) bases completas con presupuesto máximo, TRL, geografía y definición de rol de solicitante principal; (c) identificar Centro Tecnológico acreditado en procesos térmicos industriales disponible para colaboración obligatoria; (d) evaluar si proyecto de I+D propuesto alcanza 175.000 € mínimo y estructura de subcontratación 10% al Centro. Si plazo cerrado, descartar. Si plazo abierto y bases completas confirman elegibilidad, proceder a diseño de proyecto con socio tecnológico.

convocatorias.objeto_y_actuaciones: Convocatoria de ayudas para proyectos de I+D+i en industria manufacturera en Navarra, financiando investigación industrial, desarrollo experimental e innovación en procesos mediante subvención sin contraprestación. Presupuesto total 1.350.000 €. Modalidades: proyectos estratégicos (consorcio ≥3 entidades, ≥2 empresas, presupuesto >850.000 €), proyectos competitivos individuales, colaboración entre empresas (≥2 empresas, una PYME, ≥30% participación PYME), transferencia del conocimiento (PYME + agente SINAI), e innovación en procesos. Gastos elegibles: costes directos de personal, equipos, subcontratación y otros costes directos vinculados a I+D+i. Excluye: adquisición ordinaria sin innovación, actividades fuera de I+D+i, gastos no justificados. Régimen de ayudas de minimis (Reglamento UE 2023/2831).
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa posee capacidades tecnológicas sólidas en investigación industrial y desarrollo experimental de equipos térmicos (recuperadores, hornos, RTO, valorización) alineadas con INDUSTRIA MANUFACTURERA. Experiencia en proyectos I+D con TRL 4-7 compatible con alcance de la convocatoria. Sin embargo, existe un riesgo crítico de ineligibilidad: la convocatoria restringe explícitamente a ES22 (Navarra) y Kalfrisa está ubicada en Zaragoza (ES24). Debe verificarse urgentemente si esta restricción geográfica se aplica solo al coordinador o a todos los participantes. Si se permite participación como socio tecnológico desde otra región, la modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) sería la más viable. Plazo abierto hasta 2026-09-08.

Financia acciones en competitividad mediante transformación digital o tecnologías facilitadoras esenciales, innovación en diseño industrial o proceso productivo, internacionalización, marketing, optimización de cadena logística, sostenibilidad, transición energética y economía circular. Intensidades de ayuda variables según tamaño de empresa (microempresa 50-80%, empresa pequeña 40-70%, empresa mediana 30-60%) y ámbito geográfico (Huesca, T.M. Zaragoza, Resto Provincia Zaragoza, Teruel). Líneas específicas de I+D industrial, innovación en procesos y organización, derechos de propiedad industrial y consultoría estratégica con tasas de cofinanciación diferenciadas. Gastos elegibles no detallados en metadatos disponibles.
convocatorias.summary: Kalfrisa, empresa mediana manufacturera en Zaragoza, presenta alineación potencial con acciones de innovación en procesos, eficiencia energética y modernización tecnológica de la convocatoria PAIP. Línea aplicable: 'Investigación y desarrollo industrial - Empresa Mediana' (60% cofinanciación) o 'Innovación en materia de procesos y organización - Empresa Mediana' (60%), ambas sin restricción geográfica. Obstáculo crítico: metadatos SNPSAP restringen beneficiarios a PYME, mientras que tabla de intensidades incluye Empresa Mediana. Requiere verificación urgente de la orden PEJ/1052/2024 para confirmar elegibilidad. Datos faltantes: estado de convocatoria (abierta/cerrada), deadline, TRL mínimo, presupuesto mínimo de proyecto, gastos elegibles específicos, requisito de consorcio. Sin estos datos no es posible evaluar viabilidad de ejecución ni rol de Kalfrisa (beneficiaria de inversión propia vs. proveedor tecnológico).
convocatorias.action: 1. Verificar orden PEJ/1052/2024 para aclarar si empresa mediana es elegible en alguna línea o si está excluida por restricción a PYME. 2. Confirmar estado actual de la convocatoria (abierta, cerrada, ventanilla permanente) y deadline de solicitud. 3. Obtener detalle de gastos elegibles y presupuesto mínimo de proyecto. 4. Aclarar TRL mínimo/máximo y si se financia I+D, demostración, inversión en equipos o consultoría. 5. Confirmar si consorcio es obligatorio, permitido o penalizado. 6. Si elegibilidad se confirma, evaluar alineación de proyecto específico (ej. modernización de hornos, recuperación de calor, electrificación de procesos) con acciones financiables. 7. Considerar línea de 'Consultoría estratégica - Empresa Mediana' (50% cofinanciación) como alternativa de menor riesgo si proyecto aún está en fase de diseño.

convocatorias.title: GRAPPA Open Call for valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams - CUT-OFF 2
convocatorias.description: Opportunity GRAPPA Open Call for valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams - CUT-OFF 2 DEADLINE: 20 October 2026 GRAPPA call targets SME projects developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams into the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients SCOPE AND ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS This call targets innovative SMEs developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams , contributing to more sustainable and resilient agri-food ecosystems through the development of new processes, services and products. This Innovation Call includes financial support for projects especially focusing on the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients for food and non-food applications, products, business processes, and technologies (including digital) that maximise the valorisation of agri-food biomass and side-streams . These projects should have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6. The Innovation Open Call targets: SMEs in the agri-food production and/or processing sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise their own biomass/by-products/side-streams for the agri-food sector; SMEs offering solutions and/or technology for the valorisation of biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector (development and application of new technologies or processes). Applicants can be SMEs registered at EU Member States and countries associated to the Single Market Programme TIMING Launch of the Open Call: March 26, 2026 First Cut-off date: May 26, 2026 – 17:00 CET Second Cut-off date: October 20, 2026 – 17:00 CET SUBMISSION AND EVALUATION PROCESS AMENDED CALL TEXT 16 JULY 2026 : Please take into account that the Open call documentation has been updated. Submission of your proposal has to be done on the GRAPPA call website: Click here Your proposal will be submitted to an eligibility check, if all the mandatory information is completed your proposal will be evaluated. The evaluation will be done by 3 independent evaluators following a clear and transparent evaluation procedure that you can find in the Grappa open call applicant’s guide available at the call website . This evaluation period shall take place within two months after the closure of each cut-off date. Top-ranked proposals that meet the threshold scores will be awarded and contacted immediately after the final ranking and enter the Sub-Grant Agreement phase which shall last approximately one month. FURTHER INFORMATION You can consult to the GRAPPA Open Call Documentation, including the Open call applicant’s guide and Application Form at the call website For further information about this Call, you can consult the open call applicant’s guide that provide all the necessary information about this call. For more information about the overall GRAPPA project, you can consult our website and LinkedIn page . TASK DESCRIPTION The applicant’s project must lead to the implementation of either a new process, a new product, or a new service or a combination of them . Proposals can be submitted either by a single SME or by an SMEs consortium with up to three (3) SMEs . Projects must have a minimum Technology Readiness Level ( TRL ) of at least 6. The expected duration of the innovation projects is of 1 year . For Single SME projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (1 SME) is €60.000 . For collaborative projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (2-3 SMEs) is €90.000 . This call has a total budget of € 2.020.000 over both cut-off dates. Innovation grants must be matched by at least 15% private financial contribution (debt or own financial resources), with proof required. AMENDMENT 16 JULY 2026 Following aspects of the call text have been updated and clarified: Thematic priorities - scope of the call and valorisation pathways Call definitions: biosolutions added, TRL requirements clarified Documents required: no stamp needed, only signature Eligibility criteria Evaluation procedure, criteria and scoring: 2 stage evaluation process in Cut-off 2, pre-selection (knock-out stage) added. Timing of the evaluation procedure cut-off 2 prolonged Re-submission of proposals: to be done in new application form Period to file complaints SPOC contact details Pay attention that there is an adapted application form for cut-off 2! convocatorias.description: Expected Outcome: Successful proposals will contribute to the Circular Economy Action Plan, the Chemicals Strategy for Sustainability, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, the Chemical Industry Action Plan, and the Clean Industrial Deal. Projects results are expected to contribute to the following expected outcomes: Sustainable feedstock diversification for the production of bio-based polymers. Scalable process(es) for obtaining SSbD bio-based polymers from bio-based feedstock alternative to primary biomass. Enlarge the portfolio of performant bio-based polymers, opening up new market applications. Scope: Emerging alternative sources of bio-based polymers are gaining more and more attention as substitutes for primary biomass from agriculture and forestry. Additional R&I effort is needed to study innovative and scalable processes where bio-based polymers from unexplored/alternative resources are the main products. Proposals under this topic should: Develop (at TRL 5) efficient processes for synthesis and/or extraction of bio-based polymer(s) from the alternative sources in scope, targeting high yield and selectivity. Primary biomass from agriculture and forestry is out of scope; for other applicable feedstock the CBE JU Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA) [1] and its Annex V can be consulted. When relevant, develop adequate pretreatment/fractionation of targeted feedstock. Both new bio-based polymers and already established ones (but currently produced at scale from primary feedstock) are in scope. Integrate further isolation and purification (when relevant) of obtained bio-based polymer(s) according to specific application requirements. Functionalisation of purified bio-based polymers to achieve targeted properties is also in scope. Test (at least at TRL 4) the suitability of obtained bio-based polymers in circular-by-design final applications targeting at least two market sectors. Validate the technical performances of developed bio-based polymers materials/products and proving to fulfil market requirements for selected application sector(s). Test (at least at TRL 4) for suitable, safe and sustainable EoL options (recycling, biodegradation, re-use and/or re-manufacturing). When targeting biodegradable bio-based polymers, test biodegradability according to existing standards and methods. In addition to the specific requirements applicable for the type of action, as described in section 2.2.3.1 of the CBE JU Annual Work Programme 2026 [1] , proposals under this topic should: As part of the multi-actor approach (MAA), involve bio-based feedstock providers and waste management operators, end-users in targeted application sector(s) and consumers (if targeting consumer products). Include a task to apply the SSbD framework, developed by the European Commission for the assessment of targeted bio-based polymers. For more information on the SSbD framework and criteria, refer to Safe and sustainable by design . Ensure complementarities with past and ongoing R&I projects addressing similar challenges, including projects funded under Horizon 2020/Horizon Europe (under Cluster 6 and other Clusters of Horizon Europe) and BBI JU/CBE JU projects. [1] https://www.cbe.europa.eu/reference-documents [2] https://www.cbe.europa.eu/reference-documents
convocatorias.eligibility_reason: La convocatoria financia polímeros bio-basados a partir de fuentes alternativas (no biomasa primaria) con procesos de síntesis, extracción, pretratamiento y funcionalización. Kalfrisa posee capacidades en procesos térmicos industriales, recuperación de calor, combustión e hibridación, pero no consta experiencia en síntesis, extracción o funcionalización de polímeros bio-basados. El perfil de Kalfrisa se centra en equipos y procesos térmicos para sectores como cerámica, siderurgia, vidrio y química, no en desarrollo de nuevos materiales poliméricos. Aunque la convocatoria menciona 'multi-actor approach' y podría admitir proveedores de tecnología térmica para pretratamiento o postcombustión de residuos, no hay evidencia de que Kalfrisa haya participado en cadenas de valor de polímeros bio-basados ni de que sus tecnologías térmicas sean críticas para los procesos de síntesis/extracción/funcionalización descritos. Falta información sobre tipos de entidad elegibles, geografías, presupuesto, tasa de financiación y requisitos de consorcio.
